newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-VANCOUVER BEATS CALGARY TO MOVE CLOSER TO THE PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-VANCOUVER BEATS CALGARY TO MOVE CLOSER TO THE PLAYOFFS.

text.p: Trevor Linden scored for the first time in nearly a month to cap a three-goal first period and Kirk McLean stopped 28 shots as the Vancouver Canucks defeated the Calgary Flames, 5-2, on Saturday.
Sergei Nemchinov and Brian Noonan, acquired from the New York Rangers on March 8th, also scored in the first period for Vancouver.
The Canucks moved within three points of Calgary and Chicago for the final playoff berth in the West.

At the Islanders, Bryan Smolinski scored twice in a four-goal first period and Zigmund Palffy had a hat trick in the second period as the New York Islanders cruised to an 8-2 victory over the Boston Bruins.
New York improved to 4-0-1 in its last five games, its longest unbeaten streak of the season, and moved to within one point of eighth-place Washington in the Eastern Conference.
Newly-acquired Robert Reichel had four assists, giving him 12 points in five games since being acquired from Calgary.
In Hartford, Derek King and Geoff Sanderson scored first-period goals as the Hartford Whalers posted a 2-1 victory over the New York Rangers.
Sean Burke made 25 saves for Hartford.
Despite the news that the team will leave Hartford, a sellout crowd of 14,660 still showed.
Jeff Beukeboom scored the lone goal and Glenn Healy stopped 27 shots for New York, which has lost four of its last six games. All-Star centre Mark Messier did not play due to a leg injury.

In Pittsburgh, Jaromir Jagr made a successful return with two assists and Ken Wregget also returned and stopped 27 shots as the Pittsburgh Penguins snapped a three-game losing streak with a 4-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings.
Ron Francis scored two goals, including the 400th of his career, as the Penguins won for just the fifth time in their last 22 games.
In Colorado, rookies Sergei Berezin and Mike Johnson scored 49 seconds apart late in the third period and the Toronto Maple Leafs rallied to beat the Avalanche, 3-2.
Wendel Clark had the other goal for the Maple Leafs.
Valeri Kamensky and Rene Corbet scored in the second period for Colorado, which played without injured goaltender Patrick Roy and rested regulars Keith Jones and Uwe Krupp.
"There's just no drive out there," said Colorado defenceman Adam Foote. "(There's) nothing positive about this game, except that it's over."
At Florida, Tom Fitzgerald scored his first goal in more than two months with 85 seconds left in regulation, lifting the Florida Panthers into a 1-1 deadlock with the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Fitzgerald knotted the game by deflecting Terry Carkner's slap shot from the left point past goaltender Daren Puppa and just inside the left post. It was Fitzgerald's 10th goal of the season and first since January 22nd.
"It has been a long time," said Fitzgerald. "I'm a streaky scorer but I have other jobs to do than score goals."
"It was a lucky goal," Puppa said. "Anytime you tip it in the air from three feet away it's lucky."

In Ottawa, Shawn McEachern scored twice and Alexei Yashin added a goal and two assists as the surging Ottawa Senators defeated the Montreal Canadiens, 5-2, creating a logjam in the race for the final two Eastern Conference playoff berths.
Steve Duchesne and Daniel Alfredsson also scored for Ottawa.
Ottawa spotted the Canadiens a 1-0 lead before scoring the next five goals.
Only three points separate five teams battling for the final two berths.

In Washington, Eric Lindros scored twice in his return to the lineup and Ron Hextall made 21 saves as the Philadelphia Flyers increased their lead atop the Eastern Conference with a 5-3 victory over the Washington Capitals.
The Flyers moved four points ahead of idle New Jersey for the lead in the Atlantic Division and Eastern Conference.

"You get a little success on the road and you get confidence, and confidence and success breeds more success," Lindros said. "The key to any hockey team is solid goaltending and we've had that all year.
Former Flyer Rick Tocchet had a goal and an assist for Washington.

In Phoenix, Steve Kelly's first NHL goal turned out to be the game-winner and Curtis Joseph made 35 saves as the Edmonton Oilers vaulted over Phoenix into fourth place in the Western Conference with a 3-1 victory over the Coyotes.
Andrei Kovalenko and Mariusz Czerkawski also scored for Edmonton.
Dallas Drake had the lone goal for Phoenix.
